definition: Psychodynamic group psychotherapy is a form of group therapy that uses psychodynamic ideas to help people examine enduring maladaptive beliefs, habits, and emotional expectations, especially those shaped by earlier experience. The group setting adds therapeutic opportunities not available in one-to-one therapy by using interactions among members and therapists to support trust, reflection on inner experience, and meaningful change over time.

reasons: The definition includes the specific element “emotional expectations”; the packet discusses maladaptive beliefs and habits and early-life adaptations, but does not clearly support “emotional expectations” as a stated feature of psychodynamic group psychotherapy in the same terms.

The definition attributes “psychodynamic ideas” as what the therapy uses; the packet presents psychodynamic group psychotherapy but frames it primarily “through the lens of current neuroscientific concepts,” so “uses psychodynamic ideas to help…” is not directly supported in that wording.

The definition’s phrasing “trust, reflection on inner experience” is only partially supported: the packet mentions “increase epistemic trust” and mentalization/intrapersonal processes, but does not explicitly present “reflection on inner experience” in those terms.
